title: The Summit of Devil's Throat
premise: Elodie Ashgrove, a desert ranger who has spent years erasing himself from official records to escape a debt he never explains, is hired to track a thief across the empty basin called Devil's Throat. Instead of the thief, he finds a vanished government survey team, their gear intact and no tracks leading out, and a stranger named Sable Vane who claims to be the team's cartographer but remembers nothing of arriving. As the monsoon floods the Throat and traps them in a leaking boat, Elodie discovers the survey was mapping something the government wants erased: a spring whose water restores lost memories, and Sable is its living proof. The corrupt survey director returns to destroy the site and everyone who saw it, forcing Elodie to choose between staying invisible and becoming someone worth remembering; he saves Sable, exposes the director, and pays his debt at last by giving up the compass that anchored his old identity.
about_author: Freya Whitlock is a former field cartographer who spent six seasons mapping arid basins before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure stories about people the maps forgot, drawing on her years of solo expeditions and her fascination with what landscapes do to memory.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the border town of Cinder Flats, Elodie takes a contract to track a thief into Devil's Throat, hiding how little he owns and how much he owes. He burns an old letter before leaving. Emotional beat: weary self-containment, a man practicing being no one.

chapters.title: Tracks That End
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Following the thief's trail across hardpan, Elodie finds it simply stops beside fresh government survey stakes. Nearby: an abandoned camp, gear stacked neatly, cookfire still warm, no footprints leaving. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness as competence meets the impossible.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Boat
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Searching the flooded lower canyon, Elodie finds a woman adrift in a leaking survey boat with no supplies and no story she can finish. She gives her name as Sable Vane, team cartographer, but cannot recall the past week. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of mutual need.

chapters.title: What the Gear Says
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, fragmented and uncertain. Sorting the abandoned camp's instruments, Sable recognizes her own handwriting on charts of terrain she's never seen, including detailed maps of a canyon that appears on no other survey. Emotional beat: fear of one's own hand, identity unmoored.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Reading the sky, Elodie calculates they have two days before flash floods seal the Throat for weeks. They must reach the survey boat and ride it out or die walking. A distant helicopter passes over without stopping. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening trust into dependence.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The first storm hits as they run the rapids in the patched boat; Elodie steers while Sable bails. They survive by instinct and argument, wrecking a rudder but clearing the worst gorge. Emotional beat: adrenaline forging reluctant respect between strangers.

chapters.title: The Spring Beneath the Water
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Stranded on a high shelf, Sable drinks from a seep and suddenly remembers the survey team finding this place—and the director, Corvus Hale, ordering the site sealed and the team 'managed.' Her memories return in violent bursts. Emotional beat: terror and grief flooding back with the water.

chapters.title: Hale's Men
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A patrol boat flying survey colors sweeps the canyon, collecting evidence and shooting flares over side channels. Elodie realizes the search isn't for survivors—it's a cleanup. He hides their tracks for the first time not for himself, but for both of them. Emotional beat: protective instinct overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Bail and Bitterness
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Holed up in a sea cave, the pair bails water and trades truths: Elodie admits his debt is to a man he informed on, and that invisibility has been his penance. Sable accuses him of choosing cowardice. Emotional beat: conflict cracking open character, intimacy through honesty.

chapters.title: The Thief Revealed
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Tracking signs near a tributary, Elodie finally finds the thief—half-drowned, delirious, clutching a stolen sample case from the spring. The 'thief' was a junior surveyor who fled when he understood what Hale intended. Emotional beat: the hunt dissolving into rescue, moral reorientation.

chapters.title: Water That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Testing the sample, Sable realizes the spring doesn't just restore memory—it overwrites, letting whoever controls it rewrite what people know. Hale's plan becomes clear: a population that forgets on command. Emotional beat: dawning horror at power disguised as science.

chapters.title: The Junior Surveyor's Tale
chapters.summary: New character POV (the surveyor, Tomas). Delirious but lucid in stretches, Tomas recounts the team's last days: Hale dosing them, wiping the site, the escape attempt downriver. He begs Elodie to make sure someone remembers. Emotional beat: testimony as burden, the cost of witnessing.

chapters.title: Patience of the Flood
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks of monsoon confinement; food runs low, the boat rots, and Tomas worsens. Elodie teaches Sable desert craft, and she teaches him star navigation—the skills of two different kinds of survivor braided together. Emotional beat: quiet deepening of bond amid scarcity.

chapters.title: Hale Comes Downriver
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hale's main expedition arrives to finish the job, anchoring at the spring with equipment to pump and poison it. Through binoculars salvaged from camp, Sable sees a face she knows among the crew—her own brother, complicit. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deeper than danger.

chapters.title: A Plan Made of Leaks
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Outnumbered and unarmed, Elodie proposes using the failing boat itself: let the flood carry it into Hale's moorings as a drifting bomb of fuel and flare stores. Sable insists on going along to reach her brother. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing from desperation.

chapters.title: Night Run
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The night attack: they set the boat loose, cut the mooring lines in chaos, and in the confusion Sable confronts her brother, who wavers but does not turn her in. The explosion cripples Hale's pumps. Emotional beat: courage and heartbreak entwined, victory with a wound in it.

chapters.title: The Spring Runs Red
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Retreating upstream, they find Hale has poisoned the upper seep anyway—a spiteful failsafe. Tomas, drinking from it unknowingly, begins losing even his oldest memories. Emotional beat: rage and helplessness; some losses cannot be tracked and recovered.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Cornered at the canyon head, Elodie and Sable trap Hale's party against the rising flood and record his confession on the survey equipment itself, broadcasting it to the ranger network via the beacon he brought to erase signals. Hale tries to drown Elodie; Sable pulls him from the water. Emotional beat: the invisible man made unmistakably visible.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With the flood receding, authorities arrive to find everything documented: charts in Sable's hand, Tomas's recorded account, Hale's confession. Sable chooses to testify under her real name, reclaiming the identity the spring scrambled. Emotional beat: authorship of self, memory chosen rather than imposed.

chapters.title: The Debt
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The man Elodie informed on, now powerful, offers to erase the debt if Elodie stays silent about the spring's location. Elodie refuses and instead surrenders the compass—his father's, collateral held since childhood—paying what he owes with the last object tying him to his old life. Emotional beat: liberation through loss.

chapters.title: Dry Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The dry season opens the Throat again. Tomas, memory fading, asks Sable to tell him his stories each morning, and she agrees. Elodie and Sable part at the trailhead—or almost part; she hands him new coordinates, a beginning rather than an end. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin, futures sketched lightly.

chapters.title: The Summit of Devil's Throat
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, epilogue. Months later, Elodie climbs to the Throat's summit with Sable, where the spring's true source emerges above the flood line, clean and unmapped. He sketches it himself—his first map ever drawn—and signs it. Emotional beat: an invisible man placing himself, deliberately, on the map.
